mainText:
Tonga has beaten England at the Rugby League World Cup for the first time in history, while the All Blacks beat the Wallabies forty three to twenty one in Sydney despite finishing with just fourteen fit players.

New Zealand.

A body has been recovered from the water following a crash on Chapel Street, Tauranga, Bay of Plenty Police confirm. This follows a search by police divers for a second occupant after a vehicle entered the water overnight.

Thieves are targeting trailer tyres across the Bay of Plenty. Police are urging owners to secure their wheels after a spate of thefts in the region.

Fuel prices have topped four dollars a litre at the pump. An AA spokesperson says prices are expected to stay high until at least Christmas, with shipping costs on oil cargoes a factor.

On the campaign trail, the Greens have proposed abolishing the training wage, with co-leader Chloe Swarbrick saying it would mean apprentices are paid properly for their work. National has promised fewer council approvals for farms, a policy unveiled by Christopher Luxon and Todd McClay at AgFest in Greymouth. Around one hundred and sixty six thousand young people aged eighteen to twenty four remain unenrolled to vote, with get-out-the-vote efforts intensifying before polling day.

A new survey finds Māori are going without healthcare or delaying treatment because of cost and availability, as the worst flu outbreak in ten years tests the health system. Charities say close to one hundred and seventy thousand children are going without essentials on a regular basis, and are calling for sustained political action from whoever forms the next government.

Manufacturing continued to grow in September, the fifteenth consecutive month of expansion for the sector, a signal the economy is gradually strengthening heading into summer.

World.

Donald Trump has waived several sanctions on Russia, intensifying his row with President Zelensky. Republicans and Democrats have both criticised the move, saying it undermines support for Ukraine, while Italy's defence minister told the BBC Trump is completely wrong to restrict support, warning it risks prolonging the invasion.

Rwanda backed M23 rebels have entered Goma in the Democratic Republic of Congo. United Nations officials estimate more than one million displaced people are now inside the city, with residents reporting gunfire and shelling as Congolese troops were overrun.

Kenya's Ebola outbreak has risen to seven cases, including three health workers who treated the country's first confirmed patient. The World Health Organisation is monitoring the response as authorities work to contain further spread.

Pope Leo the Fourteenth has returned to the Vatican after lung cancer surgery, with his surgeon saying there are no clinical reasons to prevent his planned trip to Latin America next month. He gave the traditional Angelus blessing in St Peter's Square on Sunday.

Technology.

Anthropic is seeking new investors ahead of a planned stock market debut, the BBC reports, as some investors grow concerned about the scale of spending on artificial intelligence infrastructure. The company has not detailed a timeline for listing.

Netflix will cut around one thousand jobs, roughly six per cent of its global workforce, its steepest cuts since twenty twenty two. The company has not detailed which divisions will be most affected.

A Russian man has been arrested in Germany over the twenty twenty four hack of London hospital blood testing firm Synnovis, which disrupted patient care across the city. The twenty eight year old is accused of being part of the cyber crime gang behind the attack.

Sport.

League. Rugby League World Cup. Tonga beat England in their opening match at HBF Park, Addin Fonua-Blake's double helping secure the Pacific nation's first ever win over England. Papua New Guinea's Kumuls and the Cook Islands' Orchids both won their opening World Cup matches in Port Moresby. Samoa's women, Fetū Samoa, lost forty nil to the Jillaroos but won praise from Australia for their performance. The Kiwi Ferns open their campaign against Fiji, looking to repeat their dominant twenty twenty three campaign.

Rugby. The All Blacks beat the Wallabies forty three to twenty one in Sydney to sweep the Bledisloe Cup, finishing with just fourteen fit players after injuries, including to midfielder Jordie Barrett, ruled out before kickoff with a tight calf. Josh Moorby scored two tries. The Black Ferns beat France in the opening test of a three match series in Hamilton, scoring at better than a point a minute.

Rugby. Northland booked their first ever National Provincial Championship grand final spot, beating Otago thirty eight to nineteen in Whangārei.

Netball. The Silver Ferns begin the Constellation Cup series against the Australian Diamonds, aiming to add the trophy to their Commonwealth Games gold. Shooter Georgia Heffernan says her connection with Grace Nweke was key to the Commonwealth Games campaign.

Cycling. Great Britain's Anna Morris completed a hat-trick of gold medals at the Track Cycling World Championships in Shanghai, winning the women's madison alongside Erin Boothman.

Coming up. The Kiwi Ferns open their Rugby League World Cup campaign against Fiji. The Rugby League World Cup continues through the week. The Constellation Cup netball series against Australia continues. Tropical Cyclone Wati is tracking toward the Southern Cook Islands, with Aitutaki residents urged to heed updates as conditions deteriorate.

End of flash.
